title: Gabrielle & Riley
text:
Questions
      
      We’ve compiled a list of preliminary answers here and will update them as the day gets closer. If you have more questions, always feel free to reach out.
      The Day
      
        
        What time should I arrive?
        The ceremony begins at 5:30 pm. Please plan to arrive by 5:00 so you have time to park
        and find a seat. The reception ends at 10:30 pm.
      
        
        Is the wedding outside?
        Partly. The ceremony is outside on the lawn overlooking Cayuta Lake. If it rains, we’ll
        move it under the clear-sided tent on the patio. Cocktail hour and dancing are on the
        covered patio, and dinner is inside the Inn’s banquet hall, which has air conditioning.
        You’re welcome to step inside at any point.
      
        
        What is the dress code?
        We ask that guests wear formal attire. We suggest suits for men, and floor-length or
        tea-length dresses for women. If you have any questions, feel free to ask us. One practical
        note: the ceremony is on the lawn, so you may be more comfortable in block heels or flats.
      
      
      Guests & RSVP
      
        
        Can I bring a guest?
        Unfortunately, due to capacity limits at our venue, your invitation will name everyone
        we have saved a seat for.
      
        
        When do we need to RSVP?
        Invitations will go out in March 2027, and the RSVP deadline will be on them. You don’t
        need to do anything before then.
      
        
        I have a dietary restriction, can you accommodate?
        Yes. Please let us know when you RSVP. Our caterer, Word of Mouth, regularly handles
        vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, and allergy needs, and every dish at dinner will be
        labeled.
      
      
      Getting There
      
        
        Is there parking at the venue?
        Yes, there is plenty of free parking at the Inn if you choose to drive.
      
        
        Will there be a shuttle?
        Yes. We’re planning a shuttle from downtown Ithaca to the Inn before the ceremony and
        two trips back at the end of the night. See Travel & Stay
        for details; we’ll post pickup times closer to the wedding.
      
        
        Where should I stay?
        We aren’t holding a room block, so book whatever suits you. Our favorite hotels and
        inns are on the Travel & Stay page. If you want to use the
        shuttle, stay in downtown Ithaca.

title: Gabrielle & Riley
text:
Travel & Stay

    
      Our wedding is taking place at the Fontainebleau Inn in Alpine, New York. The Inn sits on
      Cayuta Lake, in the countryside between Ithaca and Watkins Glen.
    

  





  
    Where to Stay
    To give our guests the flexibility to stay in a range of places, we aren’t holding a room block. Here are a few spots our friends and family have stayed and loved. Airbnb and VRBO are great options too, especially for groups. We’re also offering a shuttle to and from the venue, with pickup and drop-off in downtown Ithaca.
  




  
  
  
    Downtown Ithaca
    The center of town, where the shuttle will pick up
    
        
          Canopy by Hilton
          Downtown Ithaca
          Walk to the shuttle
          On the edge of the Commons, with bright, modern rooms.
          Book now
        
        
          Ithaca Marriott
          Downtown Ithaca
          Walk to the shuttle
          Right on the Commons, and home to the new Patsy’s Pizzeria, the famous New York-style pizza place.
          Book now
        
        
          Argos Inn
          Downtown Ithaca
          Walk to the shuttle
          A 13-room boutique hotel just off the Commons, with a great cocktail bar and guest parking.
          Book now
        
  


  
  
  
    Trumansburg
    Riley’s hometown, a classic small Finger Lakes village
    
        
          16 Elm Heritage Hotel
          Trumansburg
          A small hotel just off Main Street with five rooms, some with kitchens.
          Book now
        
        
          Gothic Eves Inn
          Trumansburg
          A bed and breakfast in the middle of the village, with a spa and a great breakfast.
          Book now
        
  


  
  
  
    Watkins Glen
    A larger town on the south end of Seneca Lake
    
        
          Harbor Hotel
          Watkins Glen
          On the water at the south end of Seneca Lake, with a marina and a lakeside restaurant.
          Book now
        
        
          The Blackberry Inn
          Watkins Glen
          A quaint B&B in the village, walking distance to Seneca Lake and the state park.
          Book now
        
  




  

    

      
        Flying in
        Airports
        Ithaca Tompkins (ITH) and Elmira Corning (ELM) are the closest airports to the venue. Syracuse (SYR) is farther out, about ninety minutes away, but it often has more flights and lower fares.
      

      
        Getting around
        Rent a Car
        Downtown Ithaca, Trumansburg, and Watkins Glen are all walkable, but the surrounding area is rural, so you may want a car to explore or to travel to the venue and the welcome party. Ubers and rideshares can be hard to find out here. There is plenty of free parking at the Inn.
      

      
        On the day
        Shuttle
        We’re planning a shuttle from downtown Ithaca to the Inn before the ceremony, with two trips back at the end of the night: one around 9:30 pm and one after the reception ends at 10:30 pm. We’ll post pickup times and stops here closer to the wedding.

title: Gabrielle & Riley
text:
Things to Do

    
      We both love the Finger Lakes. Here are a few of our favorite places to eat, drink, hike, and explore while you’re in town.
    

  



  
    
      Food
      Ice Cream
      Coffee
      Wineries
      Hiking & Walking Trails
      With Kids
    
    
      

      
        Finger Lakes Cider HouseInterlaken
        Cider tastings and a menu made with food from their orchard and nearby farms. We love a slow afternoon here.
      
      
        Tabora FarmDundee
        Where we stop for lunch on the way to the Seneca Lake wineries. Soups, sandwiches, baked goods, and South African dishes.
      
      
        Main Street MarketTrumansburg
        Sandwiches, salads, local groceries, and Wide Awake Bakery bread, right on Main Street.
      
      
        New York PizzeriaTrumansburg
        Riley’s favorite New York-style pizza, right on Main Street.
      
      
        Bickering TwinsIthaca
        Tacos, birria quesadillas, and a tequila and mezcal bar.
      
      
        GorgersIthaca
        Subs, wraps, and rice bowls, with lots of vegetarian and vegan options.
      
      
        The HeightsIthaca
        A dressier dinner spot in Cayuga Heights, with a great wine list.
      
      
        Saigon KitchenIthaca
        Our favorite Vietnamese food. It’s great for takeout, too.
      
      
        Ithaca Farmers MarketIthaca
        Weekend mornings by the water at Steamboat Landing. Lots of prepared food, plus produce, bread, and cider to take home.
      
      
    
    
      

      
        Sweet Melissa’sIthaca
        Homemade hard ice cream, soft serve, and lots of vegan flavors.
      
      
        Trimmers Ice CreamTrumansburg
        A family-run shop on Route 96, close to the welcome party.
      
      
        Spotted Duck CreameryPenn Yan
        Frozen custard made with eggs from their own ducks. It’s rich, and worth the drive.
      
      
        Cayuga Lake CreameryInterlaken & Ithaca
        Homemade ice cream on Route 89 along Cayuga Lake, with a second shop in downtown Ithaca.
      
      
    
    
      

      
        Gimme! CoffeeIthaca & Trumansburg
        Ithaca’s own roaster, and the coffee we drink most.
      
      
        Press Bay AlleyIthaca
        Coffee and a handful of small shops in a converted alley off West State Street.
      
      
        Forty Weight CoffeeIthaca
        A small-batch roaster with a café in Collegetown, a counter inside GreenStar, and a stall at the farmers market.
      
      
    
    
      

      
        Hosmer WineryOvid
        Riley worked here, so we’re biased. We love their Riesling and Cabernet Franc.
      
      
        Six Eighty CellarsOvid
        Small-batch wines aged in clay and concrete, with a long view down Cayuga Lake.
      
      
        Bet the FarmTrumansburg
        A small, women-owned winery just outside Trumansburg.
      
      
        Six Mile Creek VineyardIthaca
        The closest winery to downtown Ithaca, with a distillery too.
      
      
        Hermann J. WiemerDundee
        Some of the best Riesling in the Finger Lakes. Their dry Riesling will be on the wine list at our reception.
      
      
        Dr. Konstantin FrankHammondsport
        The longest drive on this list, on Keuka Lake, and one of the oldest wineries in the region.
      
      
    
    
      

      
        Taughannock FallsTrumansburg
        A 215-foot waterfall, taller than Niagara, in the same park as the welcome party. The trail to the base is flat and shaded.
      
      
        Watkins Glen State ParkWatkins Glen
        Nineteen waterfalls along a stone gorge trail. It gets busy, so go early.
      
      
        Robert H. TremanIthaca
        Our pick for a hot day. You can swim at the base of a waterfall in the lower park.
      
      
        Buttermilk FallsIthaca
        Close to town and quick if you only have an hour. The trail is wet stone, so wear good shoes.
      
      
        Beebe Lake LoopIthaca
        An easy, shaded one-mile loop around the lake on Cornell’s campus, past a waterfall.
      
      
        Stewart Park & the Waterfront TrailIthaca
        A flat, paved path along the south end of Cayuga Lake that passes the farmers market.
      
      
    
    
      

      
        SciencenterIthaca
        A hands-on science museum for kids, with an outdoor play area.
      
      
        Ithaca Children’s GardenIthaca
        Three acres of gardens made for climbing and digging.
      
      
        Museum of the EarthIthaca
        Fossils, a full whale skeleton, and a good rainy-day plan.
      
      
        Stewart Park PlaygroundIthaca
        A big lakefront playground built for kids of all abilities. The carousel runs all summer.
      
      
        Cayuga Nature CenterIthaca
        A six-story treehouse, animals to visit, and miles of trails above the lake.
      
      
        Cornell Botanic GardensIthaca
        Free gardens and an arboretum on campus. Easy to wander with little kids, and beautiful in June.
      
      
    
  





  
    Lay of the Land
